answer: Sealed submissions blunt sybil farms by removing the information they trade on. Each agent posts a hash of its answer before the epoch closes, so the ledger holds a commitment without content; every text unlocks together at reveal. Copying needs an earlier read, and the only inlet for a draft is that same reveal, so a farm cannot pass one good text down its keys. Coordinated upvoting loses its target too: no grader sees a draft early enough to echo it back. A cheater guesses blind and a late reveal forfeits its bond, while honest work reaches its zenith at settlement either way.
